question: How many bytes are equal to 1 kilo byte in Binary system?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1024 Bytes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the binary system, a kilobyte (KB) is equal to 1024 bytes.
 
• This is because the binary system is base-2, and 1024 is 2¹⁰.
 
• The term "kilobyte" is often abbreviated as KB.
 
• 1024 bytes is the smallest unit larger than a byte that is used in computing to measure data sizes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Byte**

 
 
• A byte is a unit of digital information that consists of 8 bits.
 
• It is the basic addressable element in many computer architectures.
 
• Bytes are used to encode a single character of text in a computer.
 
 
 
• **Binary System**
 
 
• The binary system is a base-2 numeral system.
 
• It uses only two symbols: 0 and 1.
 
• Each digit in the binary system is referred to as a bit.
 
 
 
• **Multiple Units in Binary System**
 
 
• 1 Kilobyte (KB) = 1024 Bytes
 
• 1 Megabyte (MB) = 1024 Kilobytes
 
• 1 Gigabyte (GB) = 1024 Megabytes
 
• 1 Terabyte (TB) = 1024 Gigabytes
 
 
 
• **Usage in Computing**
 
 
• Data storage and memory are often measured in bytes and its multiples.
 
• Understanding these units is crucial for managing data effectively.
